follow_ups.root_analysis: keyboard/IME is on the client (Mac cmux -> sshd -> cmuxd-remote -> herdr on this host); host ibus cannot switch the client IME; Hangul IMEs hold jamo in preedit so 1:1 mapping is unreliable; Ctrl combos, digits, punctuation, arrows, Tab/Enter/Esc pass through Korean IMEs on Mac/Windows/Linux and over SSH
follow_ups.proposal: Ctrl+letter aliases after prefix, prefix Space command menu (arrows/Enter/digits), Hangul-after-prefix hint, keep existing IME-neutral keys

follow_ups.root_analysis: Mac 2-set Korean IME holds a lone jamo in preedit (marked text); cmux sends nothing over SSH until the IME commits it, so the UI never received ㅇ. Ctrl combos bypass the IME (Ctrl-] Ctrl-d works).
follow_ups.question: Ctrl-] 뒤에서 한글 키를 어떻게 처리할까요?
follow_ups.decision: after the prefix, a single Hangul compatibility jamo is converted to its 2-set (dubeolsik) QWERTY key and runs that command; the IME commit key right after it (Space/Enter) is swallowed; supersedes the earlier 'no 1:1 mapping' constraint for command keys at the user's request
